text:
The most likely corrupted element is **M7**. Its multiplier `m=3` makes it a 3:1 mirror of the reference M9, so the pc/pcd bias branch carries about 17 uA. That is roughly 7 uA more than a 1:1 mirror would give, which accounts for most of the power overage (about 12 uW at 1.8 V). M7 is also in triode (Vds 0.082 V < Vdsat 0.177 V), so it cannot hold its intended current. The strong M9 gain sensitivity (+12.9 dB) points to this same bias path, which sets the M3 gate and keeps the output-side load in triode. That explains the low gain and the high vout_dc. This is an inference from the operating points and sensitivities, not a confirmed simulation. The 1:1 alternative is my reading of the intended ratio, not something the netlist states.

M4 is second because it is in triode with Vds 0.399 V below Vdsat 0.575 V, and it eats headroom in the M3 load stack. Its sizing is also inconsistent with the other pb-network devices. M8 is third because it carries the 17 uA branch current and has a +4% power sensitivity.

The pc/pcd bias branch draws about 17 uA instead of about 10 uA, which adds roughly 12 uW of supply power and pushes the M3 load into triode, causing the gain collapse and high vout_dc.
